dedupe_keys.name: ectel annual electronic communications sector review eastern caribbean 2006 to 2024

description: The Eastern Caribbean Telecommunications Authority is the regional regulator for five contracting states: Dominica, Grenada, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines. It publishes an annual review of the electronic communications sector. The 17th edition covers April 2023 to March 2024 in 39 pages, and editions back to 2006 are in the site's media library. Each review reports revenue, investment, employment, traffic and service penetration by state, using the ITU core indicators for infrastructure and access. Data are collected through ECTEL's online data collection portal from licensed providers, coordinated by the national telecommunications regulatory commissions. Coverage: the five ECTEL states, annual totals by state, some by service and technology. Format and access: PDF reports on the ECTEL website, free; all rights reserved, so reuse of the figures needs permission. Caveats: PDF only; the fiscal year runs April to March; figures are revised in later editions; the stats page of the site is script-rendered and gave no data to a plain request. Simulation uses: subscriptions, traffic and investment series for small-island telecom demand and resilience studies, for example before and after Hurricane Maria (2017) in Dominica. Related records: data-itu-ict-statistics gives the same indicators for comparison; data-opencellid gives crowdsourced cell locations for the islands.
name: ECTEL annual electronic communications sector review (Eastern Caribbean, 2006 to 2024)
notes: Report list found through the WordPress media API of ectel.int on 2026-09-26 (editions 2006 to 2013, 2021, 2023, 2024 seen; others assumed to exist). The 2023-2024 edition was downloaded to the scratchpad, its preface read with pypdf, and deleted. The hurricane use is inferred.
